did_you_know.text: Did you know? David did not go to Judah on his own initiative: he asked the Lord whether he should go, and after receiving an affirmative answer, he asked which city to go to. The Lord told him to go to Hebron.
Did you know? After David arrived in Hebron, the men of Judah anointed him king over the house of Judah.
Did you know? David blessed the men of Jabesh-gilead for the kindness they had shown Saul when they buried him, even though Saul had been David’s rival.
Did you know? Abner son of Ner, Saul’s army commander, took Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him to Mahanaim to make him king.
Did you know? Ish-bosheth ruled over Israel for two years, while the house of Judah followed David, who ruled in Hebron for seven years and six months.
Did you know? Joab and David’s men met Abner and Ish-bosheth’s men near the pool of Gibeon, with each side sitting on the opposite side of the pool.
Did you know? Twelve men from Benjamin and twelve of David’s men fought one another, and the passage says that they all fell together at a place called the Field of Blades at Gibeon.
Did you know? Asahel, one of the three sons of Zeruiah, is described as being exceptionally swift, like a gazelle in the open field.
Did you know? Abner repeatedly warned Asahel to turn away from him, but when Asahel refused, Abner struck him with the butt of his spear, and Asahel died on the spot.
Did you know? In the battle, 360 of Abner’s men were killed, while David’s men lost 19 men in addition to Asahel. Afterward, Asahel was buried in his father’s tomb in Bethlehem.
